summary: Source-anchored research for VPC Atlas Security. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Use an Atlas private endpoint-aware connection string for endpoint traffic. Atlas recommends its DNS seedlist form so clients discover changing port assignments; standard connection strings serve other access paths. (medium confidence)
Private endpoints let applications reach Atlas through cloud-private connectivity instead of sending database traffic over the public internet. (high confidence)

For AWS PrivateLink, Atlas can assign ports in 1024-65535 and change them after cluster changes. MongoDB recommends DNS seedlist endpoint-aware connection strings and allowing the full endpoint port range rather than pinning individual ports. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-29)

Atlas private endpoints let clients initiate private connections to Atlas without allowing Atlas to initiate reciprocal connections into the client VPC; AWS describes this as preserving the network trust boundary. (medium confidence)
Atlas network guidance places dedicated clusters in a dedicated project VPC or VNet and requires TLS for database connections. (low confidence)
For VPC peering, the customer and Atlas address ranges must not overlap; address planning is a prerequisite for the private route. (medium confidence)

Enabling private endpoints does not disable other Atlas access methods: public IP access-list entries and network peering can coexist. A private-only design must separately review and remove unwanted public access permissions. (medium confidence)

Private network reachability does not replace database authentication. AWS guidance lists authentication integrations separately from private connectivity, and the PrivateLink walkthrough still requires a database user. (medium confidence)
Clients must select the private endpoint-aware connection string to use the endpoint path; the AWS and Confluent walkthroughs configure a private connection explicitly. (medium confidence)

MongoDB architecture guidance recommends private endpoints for staging and production; Confluent independently recommends private networking for production integrations handling sensitive data. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-20)

In the October 2021 Terraform issue #590, creating a second endpoint service in the same Atlas project and AWS region returned PRIVATE_ENDPOINT_SERVICE_ALREADY_EXISTS_FOR_REGION. A maintainer demonstrated referencing the existing endpoint service for multiple interface endpoints. This is historical troubleshooting evidence, not proof of an unresolved current defect. (low confidence)

Macquarie Bank engineers reported that incorrect peering configuration could expose internal services to Atlas and that mitigating the network trust risks added firewall and VPN operational complexity. (low confidence)
For Atlas integrations, private networking provides an alternative to public-IP access listing; Confluent recommends private connectivity for production and sensitive data. (medium confidence)

Network isolation does not replace database identity controls. Atlas requires TLS for database connections, and the AWS PrivateLink walkthrough still authenticates with a database user. (medium confidence)

Atlas documents private endpoint support for dedicated M10-or-higher clusters. An endpoint's provisioned status alone therefore does not establish that a particular cluster tier can use it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-29)

Confluent's 2020 walkthrough demonstrates a managed Atlas connector using a customer VPC and PrivateLink without opening Atlas to 0.0.0.0/0; its 2026 guidance instead describes public connectivity through specific Confluent egress IP allowlisting. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-20)

Validate the database connection from the intended application network after provisioning. The AWS walkthrough tests both successful access through its endpoint and failed access from an unconnected VPC; Atlas guidance recommends regular connectivity health checks. (medium confidence)
